clue.text: Self-taught chap used to work on car

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece placed on another follows it, so the working words come after the car

parts.note: auto is a short word for a motor car
'used to' describes past habit, which the auxiliary did can also express ('I did go there')
to work, of a device or plan, is to act or function

explanation.surface: A man who taught himself mechanics once spent his days tinkering with a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chap' makes the definition a person, so the answer is a noun; 'used to work' reads as a phrase about past jobs but splits into two short pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An autodidact is a person who has educated himself without teachers, the Greek roots meaning self and teaching.

clue.text: Excited by Italian wine — red, to start

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy

indicators.note: 'to start' asks for only the opening letter of the word red

explanation.surface: Someone is stirred up by Italian wine, starting on the red.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in a state of stirring activity or excitement.

clue.text: US academic session on neat chemical

parts.note: neat and trim both mean tidy and well kept
an ester is an organic chemical compound formed from an acid and an alcohol

explanation.surface: An American college term is spent studying an unmixed chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' suggests an undiluted chemical but here means tidy, giving TRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: American colleges often divide the year into three terms, each of which is called by this name.

clue.text: Despair seen here, hesitating over move in game

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece over another stands above it, so the hesitating word comes first

parts.note: doubting means wavering or hesitating to believe
to castle is a move in chess in which king and rook change places

explanation.surface: A gloomy player hesitates before making a move in a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: Despair is Giant Despair of Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, who imprisons Christian and Hopeful in his stronghold; the capital is hidden at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Pilgrim's Progress, Giant Despair lives in and rules this fortress, where he holds the pilgrims captive.

clue.text: Fanatic to be executed, that's certain

parts.note: a person executed is put to death, so is made to die
hard can mean definite and certain, as in hard facts or hard evidence

explanation.surface: A zealot is sure to be put to death.
explanation.definitionFit: A die-hard is a stubborn, uncompromising supporter of a cause, much like a zealot.

clue.text: Internationals stuck on brown turner

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece stuck on another sits on top of it, so the internationals precede the brown

parts.note: a player chosen for his country is awarded a cap, so internationals are caps
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Players capped for their country are fixated on a brown lathe operator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turner' looks like a person at a lathe but is a machine that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a revolving drum on a ship used to wind in cable, so it is something that rotates.

clue.text: Pack in point-to-point

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
W, west, is another compass point

explanation.surface: Someone loads a horse box at a point-to-point, an amateur steeplechase meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur horse race across country; here it is read as one compass point, the word to, and another.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow something is to pack it away neatly in a storage space.

clue.text: Look back along flare-path for some illumination

indicators.note: looking back means reading the tucked-away letters from right to left
the letters run along inside the word flare-path, so the wanted ones are tucked inside it

explanation.surface: Someone checks the lit runway behind them for some light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look back' turns REPAT, found inside 'flare-path', into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a thin candle or wax-coated wick giving a little light.

clue.text: Drudge has painting, perhaps, to mount

parts.note: a painting is an example of a work of art
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A hard-working labourer has a picture to put in a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' suggests framing a picture, but it is a riding animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A workhorse is someone who does a great deal of hard, tedious labour, like a drudge.

clue.text: Viola makes nothing, being unemployed

parts.note: love means nil, a score of nothing in tennis
someone without work is living with no occupation, idle

explanation.surface: A viola player earns nothing because they are out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viola' looks like the instrument, but it is the plant genus that includes pansies.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old name for the wild pansy, a member of the violet genus, used by Shakespeare for the flower whose juice causes love.

clue.text: True bit disguised in fulsome praise

indicators.note: disguised means the letters of true bit are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A grain of honesty is masked within lavish compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is an act or speech expressing high admiration and gratitude, a form of eulogy.

clue.text: Do well to get round this magician

indicators.note: the answer needs a round letter added to it to get the magician, so the magician less that round letter gives the answer

parts.note: Prospero is the magician of Shakespeare's The Tempest
O is a round letter

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to succeed by winning over a conjuror.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as answer + round = this magician: Shakespeare's Prospero without his final O.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or flourish, to succeed in life.

clue.text: One enlisting again has turned in

definitions.meaning: someone who signs up for a second time is one who enters again
an angle pointing inwards, as in a fortification or a coastline, has this description

explanation.surface: A man joining up again has handed himself over to the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned in' suggests giving oneself up or going to bed, but means pointing inwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-entrant names a person who returns and joins again, and also an angle that points inwards rather than out.

clue.text: Hole in the ground

definitions.meaning: a fox's burrow, its den in the hillside

explanation.definitionFit: A fox's den is called its earth, and earth also means soil or the land beneath our feet.

clue.text: Club fail to declare

definitions.meaning: a short stick or truncheon used as a weapon
in cricket a captain who does not declare the innings closed lets his side carry on batting

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side may declare, ending its innings early; not doing so is to bat on.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a policeman's truncheon, a kind of cudgel, and to bat on is to keep batting instead of closing the innings.

clue.text: Educationist meets a colleague of husband

parts.note: a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teaching degree, so its holder is an educationist
a fellow is a companion or associate, as in a fellow worker

explanation.surface: A teacher meets a co-worker of her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; the definition is the last word. BEd is the British teaching degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse shares a bed with his partner, so a husband is a bedfellow, one who sleeps beside another.

clue.text: Fast-food outlet?

parts.note: read not as a burger bar but as a place serving food aboard a fast-moving train

explanation.definitionFit: A dining car is a railway carriage where passengers are served meals as the train speeds along.

clue.text: Treble hit scorer got wrong

indicators.note: got wrong means the letters of hit scorer are put into an incorrect order

explanation.surface: A three-goal haul was credited to the wrong player by the scorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treble' suggests a hat-trick of goals, but it is a boy soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble is a boy with a high singing voice in a church choir, which is what a chorister often is.

clue.text: Organise strike that'll achieve aim unerringly

parts.note: to direct is to manage or organise
a hit is a blow or strike

explanation.surface: A commander plans an attack that will land exactly on target.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct hit is a shot or bomb striking precisely on its target, with no miss.

clue.text: Monopolise the bath? Nonsense!

parts.note: to hog something is to keep it all to oneself
a bath is a wash

explanation.surface: Someone protests at a housemate hogging the bathroom: rubbish!
explanation.definitionFit: Hogwash is pig swill, and so worthless talk, rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: West End price demanded in bar

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of the word West

parts.note: a ransom is the price demanded for releasing a captive

explanation.surface: A London theatre-district pub charges extortionate prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatre district, but it is the end of 'West'.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a horizontal crossbar, as above a door or across a window.

clue.text: Cheated out of a run -that's the buzz

indicators.note: the cheated word stands outside the run, so the run is held within it

parts.note: done is slang for cheated or swindled
R is the abbreviation for run, as on a cricket scoresheet

explanation.surface: A batsman robbed of a run hears the gossip about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' puts DONE around R; 'the buzz' is a humming sound, not gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a low continuous humming noise, like that of bees.

clue.text: Distinctive attitude of the dissolute and fat

indicators.note: dissolute means loose, so the letters of the word the are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: OS, outsize, is the clothing abbreviation for a fat size

explanation.surface: Some people have a characteristic outlook of debauchery and plumpness.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit and outlook of a person, group or culture.

clue.text: Philosopher dismisses English cricketer

indicators.note: dismisses means sending away the letter for English from the philosopher's name

parts.note: Thomas Hobbes was the English philosopher who wrote Leviathan

explanation.surface: A thinker gets an English batsman out.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Hobbs was a celebrated English opening batsman; 'dismisses' plays on getting a batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jack Hobbs was a Surrey and England batsman of the early twentieth century, one of cricket's greatest.

clue.text: Even a prig could be a passer-on of gossip

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of even a prig might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: Even a prudish person may spread rumours.
explanation.definitionFit: The grapevine is the informal network by which rumours and gossip pass from person to person.

clue.text: Make over money to old wife after death

indicators.note: the old wife comes after the death, so its letters follow

parts.note: end means death, the end of life

explanation.surface: A will leaves money to an elderly spouse after a death.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give a sum of money or property to someone, often as a permanent income.

clue.text: Plant daggers in Capone's back

indicators.note: the daggers go in, inside the gangster's reversed first name
back means the gangster's name is read from right to left

parts.note: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster
obeli are dagger symbols used in printing as reference marks

explanation.surface: Someone plants knives in a Chicago gangster's back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns AL into LA, which holds OBELI; 'Plant' looks like a verb but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden flowering plant, often blue, used in borders and hanging baskets.

clue.text: Not hungry, but we went in and cooked

indicators.note: the word we went in, entering the word for not hungry

parts.note: sated means satisfied, fully fed

explanation.surface: We were full, but went into the kitchen and made a meal anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweat vegetables is to cook them gently in fat so they soften without browning.

clue.text: Want quiet on Caribbean islands

indicators.note: in an across clue the piece put on another follows it, so the quiet comes after the islands

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for the West Indies
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone longs for peace and quiet on a Caribbean holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something is to desire it, to long for it.

clue.text: Seeks a ride with the gang — an agonising squash

parts.note: a hitchhiker thumbs a lift, seeking a ride
a crew is a gang, as of workers or friends

explanation.surface: A hitchhiker travels with a gang; the cramped car is a torture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' suggests a crowded car, but it is an instrument of torture that crushes the digits.
explanation.definitionFit: This medieval torture device crushed a victim's fingers by turning a screw, an excruciating squeeze.
